citations.narrative:
One newly-weaned juvenile deer mouse died from food deprivation. On July 14, 2025, animal caretaker staff discovered a
dead male deer mouse in a cage without food. Subsequent investigation revealed the mouse was weaned on July 10,
2025 by laboratory personnel that failed to provide food for the animal. DLAR staff subsequently failed to identify the
missing food during animal checks between July 11-13, 2025.
Failure to provide each animal with the proper amount of food and nutritional value needed can result in deterioration of
the animal's health to the point of expiration. The food shall be wholesome, palatable, and free from contamination and of
sufficient quantity and nutritive value to maintain all animals in good health. The diet shall be prepared with consideration
for the age, species, condition, size, and type of animal. Animals must be fed at least once a day except as dictated by
hibernation, veterinary treatment, normal fasts, or other professionally accepted practices.
The facility corrected prior to this inspection on July 15, 2025.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
